grade_inflation: **Question bank 7/10 — the single most inflated grade on the board, and it is Alex's #1 brief item.** The area's own findings list reads: the newest, Home-featured, NEW-badged pack (Summer 2026) 'ships OUTSIDE every guard the team built and leaks in 38.4% of sessions'; 'audit-leaks-full.mjs's 0 unguarded is a self-confirming zero'; '15 club-pack questions whose exact answer is the club you picked'; '5 stems contain their own answer verbatim, 21 more contain every content word of it'; '1,060 questions have no explanation'. Area 3 independently found ~36 giveaways and measured the report rate RISING (46.9→64.3 per 1,000 plays). Four highs plus a rising player-complaint rate is not a 7. And the movement rationale — 'the bank did not get worse, the measurement got better' — is a self-protective frame: the leak guard the brief credits as shipped is blind to the pack on the Home screen, which is crediting work that does not reach the content players actually see. Suggested 6.0.

**Accessibility 7/10, moved UP 0.5, while carrying two live high-severity defects that hit 100% of users on every platform.** Finding 1: 'Settings shows Timer and Show Hints as OFF while the game runs them ON — and both switches emit invalid ARIA.' Finding 2: 'Three of the four primary navigation tabs sit at 2.52:1 contrast' — that is the bottom nav, on every screen, failing AA by a wide margin. The half-point rise is credited to h1/announcer/focus-restore work, all of which is invisible to sighted users, while the two things a real person hits are unchanged. That is movement bought by inaction on the visible half. Note the Settings-toggle bug was found independently by THREE areas (a11y finding 1, Feel finding 6, and it is the same App.jsx:9530-9537 `setSettings(s)` line) — convergence that says it is real and that the grade should reflect it.

**Retention 5.5, moved UP from 5, while discovering the instrument is broken.** Its own critical: '`scores` under-records ~20% of daily completions every day — so every retention number we steer by is wrong.' You cannot claim a half-point of improvement in the same breath as finding your measurement is 20% off. The other two criticals — '39% of accounts never finish a single game, and not one of them ever comes back' and 'the outcome of a player's FIRST Footle swings retention by 20 points, 47% of first Footles end badly' — are worse than anything in report #2's retention section. Suggested hold at 5.0.

**Stability & release safety 6.5** with a critical reading '`npm run verify:native` green-ticks a native bundle 3 commits stale' plus a high reading 'the quiz engine, the results screen, Footle, Club Quiz and League Quiz are all OUTSIDE the 12 error boundaries.' The brief's shipped list credits 'error boundaries 4→12'. Twelve boundaries that do not wrap the five most-played surfaces is the textbook case of crediting work that reaches nobody. Add 'every native build carries its PARENT commit as the Sentry release' and there is no route from a crash to a diagnosis on the platform holding ~95% of native users. 6.5 is a passing grade for a release-safety area whose release verifier is broken. Suggested 5.5.

**Trust & fairness 7/10** whose own last finding is, verbatim, 'Nothing I could check in this area is true for anyone on the App Store or Play right now.' The area then grades 7 anyway. Its two highs are on the flagship mode: 'The Daily 7 review shows what you got wrong and never why — and has no report button' and 'Hot Streak gives you 1.8 seconds to read a 6.3-second explanation, then never shows it again and gives you no way to complain.' A trust area cannot grade 7 while the most-shared screen in the app withholds the explanation and the complaint channel. Suggested 6.0.

**First run 6.5.** The area's headline is the Footle hero subtitle, and it graded the card on the string alone. I played the same card on live prod and it is worse than reported (see panel_missed #1) — the same card renders a fake SOLVED board. Grading the most-viewed card in the app on one line of its copy, while the grid beside that line is showing a green winning row that is not the player's, is the same reading-not-playing failure the brief was written to stop.

I grepped the whole tree: `src/marketing/FootleBand.jsx:192` ('Guess the footballer's surname in six'), `:212` ('a {LEN}-letter surname'), `:265` ('In the surname, wrong place'), `:272`, `:273`; `src/marketing/MarketingHome.jsx:930` ('Guess the surname in six.'), `:942` (FAQ: "guess the footballer's surname in six tries"); `src/marketing/ScoutingReport.jsx:47` (same FAQ). That is 8 more live, user-facing instances on the SEO landing surface that per the project's own GSC read carries roughly half of all impressions. Area 6 counted them; Area 1 — the one whose quick_win Alex will act on — declared the fix complete at six call sites. Someone has ALREADY applied the one-line FootleHero edit in the working tree (uncommitted, `git status` shows ` M src/components/FootleHero.jsx` plus a new `tests/unit/footle-prompt-copy.test.js`) — so the wrong half is about to be marked done and guarded by a test that will pass.

I curled prod: it now serves `assets/GameRoot-L6LM0WGH.js`. Prod redeployed during/after the review window (182d64c, a4c572b and the build-76 bump all landed). The findings themselves survive — I re-grepped the CURRENT prod bundle and 'Surname of a footballer' is still there, count 1 — but the panel's confidence language ('curl'd prod and grepped, not trusting the deploy') is durable-sounding evidence about a snapshot that expired the same night.

**The build number the whole panel reasons about is stale.** The brief said '1.7.0 (iOS build 74 / vc29)'. Repo is at `CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION = 76` / `versionCode 31` (commit 3dbcafa, Aug 23 23:26). Area 3 built an entire finding on artifact timestamps — 'iOS assets built 22:21 and the AAB 22:22, both after the 21:27 commit — it is in build 74 and vc29, neither uploaded' — which is now reasoning about a superseded artifact. **'The duty is to ask before tracking' — asserted, not checked, and it points the wrong way.** Area 1 recommends widening `onboardingUp()` in public/consent.js so the banner stays suppressed until a game is completed, on the stated grounds that nothing tracks meanwhile, and cites 'I watched for clarity.ms requests across every run and counted 0.' So the recommendation would extend server-side pseudonymous tracking-without-consent from 'the taster' to 'the entire first session'. This is a compliance change proposed on an unverified premise.

**'A four-line change at four call sites' (Area 3, the premature '✓ Reported — thanks').** The defect is real — I read it: App.jsx:3102-3111, `onReport(...)` then `setReportedKeys(...)` fire synchronously in the same onClick, and `reportQuestion` (9327) only calls `setReportPending` and `return true`. But `setReportedKeys` is declared at App.jsx:2420 inside QuizEngine, with `rkey` local to the option; `sendQuestionReport` is declared at AppInner scope (9340) and invoked from the sheet at 12294. There is no wiring between them. Making the button honest means threading a promise or a pending key back through QuizEngine, WrongAnswersReview, FootleReportButton and TransferTrail. Calling that a quick win invites exactly the 'shipped in one half' failure the panel keeps citing.

**Line numbers across the visual-craft area are systematically 26 lines stale** (`.opt` cited at app.css:598, actually 624; `.feedback` cited at 630, actually 656). app.css moved under them (182d64c). Not a wrong finding — I verified `.feedback{...border:none !important;background:transparent !important}` at 656 does suppress the tinted `.feedback.wrong` at 658 — but every line reference in that area needs re-resolving before anyone edits from it.
panel_missed: **THE MOBILE FOOTLE HERO SHOWS A FAKE SOLVED BOARD. Six areas discussed this card; every one stopped at the subtitle.** I played live prod at 375x812 and read the DOM. The card renders `fh-row` KROOS (grey/yellow/grey/green/green) then `fh-row` RAMOS — five tiles ALL GREEN, a winning row — beside a CTA reading `Continue · 1/6 used`. My actual state was `biq_wordle_2026-08-24 = {"guesses":["MODRIC"],"status":"playing"}`. So the app's most-viewed card displays someone else's solved puzzle as if it were yours. Source confirms it is deliberate decoration: `TEASER_PAIRS[getWordleDayIndex() % ...]` at FootleHero.jsx:101. Worse, the same file's comment admits the knock-on: 'No letter count here ... the teaser grid to the right is hard-coded 5 wide, so on any non-5-letter day the card printed "4 letters" beside five tiles and contradicted itself.' Today's word is 6 letters. So the mobile card (a) shows a fake win, (b) shows 5 tiles for a 6-letter word, and (c) withholds the letter count — while the desktop hero in the same DOM reads 'Daily · Footle / 6 letters · 6 guesses / The name a footballer goes by' and is correct on all three. The panel's grade for this card rests entirely on fixing one string on it.

**Nobody ran a native binary. Not one of fourteen areas.** ~95% of the native base is iOS (device_tokens 35:2 per Area 2), the brief's central question is what store reviewers see, and every single 'who can see this now' answer routes to 'upload iOS'. The not_verified sections are honest about it individually — 'I never ran the NATIVE ask', 'I did not build, install or run build 74 / vc29', 'Everything here is a desktop Chromium at 375x812' — but collectively it means the panel graded a store-rating question without ever seeing the artifact the store serves. There is an `mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator` tool available in this environment and no area used it.

**Nobody signed up, so the signup wall — Area 3's own CRITICAL — is source-read only.** Area 3 calls the Apple/Google username step 'a non-dismissible dead end ... 500+ downloads are walking into it' and rates it critical, then states 'I never signed up, so I never saw UsernameSetupModal render.' The panel's highest-severity finding of the round was never observed. Nobody would need a device for this — a web signup would do it.

**Nobody played Footle to a LOSS.** Area 4 flags it ('the biggest hole in this report'), Area 6 and Retention both build findings on it (38% of Footle days end in a loss; 'the outcome of a player's FIRST Footle swings retention by 20 points'), and the fix list includes marking a loss as a bad review moment. The single most bruising two minutes in the product, named as retention-critical by two areas, was never experienced by anyone.

**Nobody typed on a real on-screen keyboard.** Three consecutive reports now say this is untested; the repo's own memory names it as the root of two shipped bugs in Trail; commits a4c572b ('the viewport never shrinks on native — that broke ALL of it') and 182d64c ('three things grabbed at the same drag') landed IN THIS WINDOW and touch exactly that code plus `tests/unit/keyboard-gesture-ownership.test.js`. Brand-new keyboard code shipped during the review and the panel has no coverage of it at all.

**The panel has no synthesis and no single answer to Alex's question.** Fourteen areas each nominate their own top item as the highest-leverage act ('the single highest-value act available', 'the highest-value change in the report', 'the highest value-to-effort change'). The brief explicitly forbids 'a list of 83 items ranked by nothing' — the panel produced 14 lists of ~8 items each, ranked by nothing across areas. The one item five areas independently converge on (upload iOS) is the one nobody verified the state of.
dangerous_recommendations: **WOULD SILENTLY DELETE THE APP'S ENTIRE CELEBRATION LAYER — Feel, quick win #2: 'add a second effect keyed on `screen` that clears the celebrationTimeoutsRef array.'** I traced this. `setScreen("results")` is the LAST statement of `handleComplete` (src/App.jsx:10822), in the same synchronous callback that pushes every celebration timer: 10559/10562/10565 (7/30/100-day streak toasts + confetti), 10571 (perfect round), 10601 (native review ask), 10607/10614 (personal-best toasts), 10620 (comeback), 10625 (category mastery), 10631 (survival record), 10651 (rate prompt), 10690 (guest save-your-progress nudge), 10796 (`setChallengeResult` — the friend-challenge result payload). A `useEffect(..., [screen])` that clears the array fires on the very commit produced by that handler, AFTER the pushes. Every one of those timers dies. Following this quick win removes: all streak milestone celebrations, the perfect-round toast, every personal-best toast, the daily-complete sound (10306), the challenge result screen, and the guest conversion nudge — while Area 6 (Delight, 5.5) is simultaneously arguing the celebration layer is already too thin. This is the report-#3-critic-grade catch of this round.

**WOULD DESYNC THE FROZEN DAILY — First run, quick win #4: 'src/lib/quiz.js:159 — add a first-session branch that does not apply `q.diff !== "easy"` when the player has no completed games.'** Line 159 is inside `pickDailyFresh`, whose own comment three lines above reads: 'Exported so the log GENERATOR can compute fresh days — it must never call pickDailyQuestions, which reads the log first and would therefore rebuild the log from itself. (That exact mistake produced a no-op regeneration on 2026-08-19.)' Branching that function on per-player state means the generator emits one Daily 7 and the client draws another: the frozen answer log stops matching what players see, the Daily 7 stops being the same set for everybody, and `record_challenge_event` (App.jsx:10791, which compares `p_score` against `p_my_score`) starts comparing scores on different question sets. The project's own memory records DAILY SCHEDULES MUST BE FROZEN as binding, from a bug that hit Footle, Trail AND the Daily 7. The area hedges in prose ('that is a design decision for Alex') and then ships the edit as a numbered quick win anyway. It also misses the SECOND site of the identical filter at quiz.js:128 (`pickDailyFromLog`'s refill) — so applied literally it produces the exact half-fix drift the panel spends 14 areas complaining about.

**WOULD DISABLE SENTIMENT SUPPRESSION FOR MOST REPORTS — Rating ask, quick win #3: 'move markBadReviewMoment() out of reportQuestion() and into sendQuestionReport(), gated on reason being wrong-answer | unclear | typo.'** `sendQuestionReport` is called with `reason = null` from `onSkip` (App.jsx:12295) and from backdrop/Escape dismiss, and the code comment at 9333 says so explicitly: 'dismissing still reports, with reason null, because the tap on "Report" is itself the signal.' Area 3 independently establishes that the null path is the one players are actively pushed toward, because the button flips to '✓ Reported — thanks' before the sheet is answered. So this change stops suppressing the rating ask for the majority of the report channel — inverting the protection the same area calls its own critical finding. Two areas' recommendations are in direct conflict and nobody reconciled them. If the reason-gating is wanted, it must default to suppressing on null, not on a whitelist.

**WOULD EXTEND TRACKING-WITHOUT-CONSENT TO THE WHOLE FIRST SESSION — First run, quick win #3: 'public/consent.js:175 — widen onboardingUp() to also suppress while no game has been completed.'** Justified on 'the duty is to ask before tracking, not to ask immediately.' But `loopEvent` (src/App.jsx:2029) has no consent gate — only `isSyntheticTraffic()` — and writes `p_visitor: visitorId()` to the prod `record_funnel_event` RPC. `onboard-done-answered` fires from it at App.jsx:7346 during onboarding. The area's own proof ('I watched for clarity.ms requests and counted 0') covers Clarity and not the funnel. This is a GDPR-surface change proposed without checking what already fires. Do not apply it without first gating loopEvent on consent — at which point the retention area's request for six MORE funnel events also needs the same gate.

**UNDER-SPECIFIED, WILL SHIP SOMETHING UGLIER — Visual craft: 'delete the two `!important`s at app.css:630 ... the highest-value two-character deletion in the codebase.'** The rule is at 656 now, and the diagnosis is correct — I confirmed `.feedback{border-radius:0;border:none !important;background:transparent !important;padding:2px 2px}` suppresses the tinted `.feedback.wrong` at 658. But deleting only the two `!important`s restores a 1px border and a tint onto an element with `border-radius:0` and `padding:2px 2px`, i.e. a hard-cornered strip with 2px of breathing room — not the designed tray. There is also a SECOND `.feedback` declaration at app.css:1600 setting `justify-content:space-between` against the base's `flex-start`, and a third at 2248 for `.qd-play`. Restore the padding, radius and reconcile the duplicate in the same edit, or this lands worse than the current naked line.
five_star_framing_verdict: Mostly answered, and better than report #3 — but the panel answers it fourteen times and never once. Quoting Alex back: "grade us on things that actually decide if people give you a 5 star or 4 star... what we should be doing to improve our current product, how we should be thinking going forward." Individually, the five_star_path sections are strong and specific, and several are genuinely category-aware rather than generic: Area 3 names the real star-loser list (repeats, wrong questions, ads, paywalls, crashes, ran-out-of-content) and scores us honestly against it — four of six clean, which IS the answer to "what have we already won"; Area 4 correctly identifies that nobody writes "missing :active state" in a review, they write "feels a bit basic"; Area 2's "a rating is a receipt for a good week, not a good second" is the right frame for a product with 56% day-1 churn. Alex's "include all the things users care about, not just the functional stuff" is genuinely served — feel, visual craft, delight and trust all exist as areas and all found real defects. Three failures, though. FIRST: no synthesis. Fourteen areas each declare their own item highest-leverage ("the single highest-value act available", "the highest-value change in the report", "the biggest feel-per-character change"). Alex asked what to DO; he gets fourteen competing #1s and ~110 quick wins. That is the "list ranked by nothing" the brief forbids, wearing a different shape. SECOND: the one recommendation five areas converge on — upload iOS — is repeated without anyone checking that the build they were briefed on (74/vc29) was superseded by 76/vc31 before the panel finished, or opening the binary. "Ship it" is not a finding when nobody looked at what would ship. THIRD: "brick by brick... methodical and follow the data" is honoured in the small (real prod queries, real controls, honest false-positive rates — Area 5's 35%, Area 4's 64%, Area 3's seed-tested detector) and violated in the large: three areas independently found the SAME bug (App.jsx:9530 `setSettings(s)` discarding the defaults merge) and none of them noticed the other two, which is the panel doing to itself exactly what it criticises the codebase for. On the question bank specifically — Alex's loudest sentence, "i really want our question bank to be spotless and not insult the intellect of our users" — the panel does answer it, twice and consistently (Area 3's ~36 giveaways at ~85% hand-reviewed precision, Area 6's 5 verbatim + 21 near-verbatim self-answering stems, the 15 club packs whose answer is the club, the 53-54% of reports filed by players who answered CORRECTLY). That convergence from independent routes is the most trustworthy result on the board. It just carries a 7/10, which contradicts it.
biggest_hole: **Fourteen areas, 500+ downloads, ~95% of the native base on iOS — and not one reviewer launched a native build.** The brief's central question is what makes someone tap five stars in the App Store. The panel answered it entirely from a desktop Chromium at a 375x812 viewport. Every area's "who can see this now" ends at "nobody until upload", and every area's top recommendation is some version of "upload iOS", and nobody opened the thing that would be uploaded — despite an iOS Simulator tool being available in this environment and the repo carrying a `ball-iq-native-build` skill. The consequences are concrete, not theoretical: Area 3's CRITICAL (the non-dismissible Apple/Google signup dead end) was never observed because nobody signed up; Area 2's entire native ratings analysis is "reasoning from the API contract and the code, not from a device"; Area 4 never felt a haptic or heard a tone; the on-screen keyboard is untested for the third consecutive report even though a4c572b ("the viewport never shrinks on native — that broke ALL of it") and 182d64c landed DURING the review window and touch exactly that code. The panel therefore cannot distinguish "1.7.0 fixes this" from "1.7.0 ships a new native regression", which is the only question that matters when the recommendation is to push a build to 500+ installed devices. The second half of the hole is the panel's own instrument: the Browser pane runs tabs HIDDEN (I confirmed `document.visibilityState === "hidden"` and `requestAnimationFrame` not firing within 500ms on my own session), which faked a 3.3s cold start for one reviewer, faked a suppressed consent banner for another, and faked three localStorage findings — all caught, to their credit, but only by reviewers who happened to run controls. The Speed area's quick win asking for this to be written into docs/SCOUTING-REPORT-BRIEF.md is the most valuable process item in the whole panel and it is buried at position six of six in one area's list.

Moved UP 0.5 while carrying two live highs that affect every user on every platform: Settings lying about Timer/Show Hints state with invalid ARIA, and three of four primary nav tabs at 2.52:1 contrast. The half-point is credited entirely to h1/announcer/focus work that sighted users cannot perceive. A 7 on trust is not compatible with the most-shared screen in the app withholding both the explanation and the complaint channel.

The area's headline finding graded the Footle hero card on one line of its subtitle. Playing the same card on live prod at 375x812 shows it also renders a hard-coded teaser board (TEASER_PAIRS, FootleHero.jsx:101) — KROOS then an all-green RAMOS row — beside a CTA reading 'Continue · 1/6 used' while real state is {guesses:['MODRIC'],status:'playing'}, and it withholds the letter count that the desktop hero in the same DOM shows correctly.
